Title: Verify that service category name handles special characters and script tags securely
Steps:
1. Authenticate as an admin user. 2. Send a POST request to /api/categories with the payload in testData. 3. Send a PUT request to /api/categories/{id} (where {id} is a newly created category) with the payload in testData.

Test Data: {"name": "Category<script>alert('xss')</script>", "description": "Description with special chars !@#$%^&*()", "status": true, "serviceType": "salon"}
Expected Result: 1. The API responds with HTTP status 400 Bad Request or sanitizes the input and creates the category with a sanitized name. The response does not execute the script. 2. The API responds with HTTP status 400 Bad Request or sanitizes the input and updates the category with a sanitized name. The response does not execute the script.

Title: Verify that rapid successive requests to add service categories are rate-limited to prevent abuse
Steps:
1. Authenticate as an admin user. 2. Send 11 successive POST requests to /api/categories with unique names for each request within a short timeframe (e.g., 1 second per request).

Test Data: {"name": "Category_N", "description": "Description", "status": true, "serviceType": "salon"} (where N is 1 to 11)
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests for the 11th and subsequent requests, or the 11th request is rejected with an appropriate error message. No more than 10 service categories are created within the defined rate limit period.

Title: Verify that service category responses do not expose internal or sensitive fields
Preconditions: A service category exists. User is authenticated with 'ROLE_ADMIN'.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as an admin user. 2. Send a GET request to /api/categories. 3. Send a GET request to /api/categories/{id} for an existing category. 4. Send a POST request to /api/categories with valid data. 5. Send a PUT request to /api/categories/{id} with valid data.

Test Data: {"name": "Test Category", "description": "Test Description", "status": true, "serviceType": "salon"}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 OK (or 201 Created for POST). The response body for each service category contains only business fields ('id', 'name', 'description', 'status', 'serviceType') and does NOT include raw audit fields like 'createdDate', 'updatedDate', or any other internal system details.

Title: Verify that adding a service profile with a non-existent category ID is rejected
Preconditions: A shop with ID 1 exists. User is authenticated with 'ROLE_ADMIN'.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as an admin user. 2. Send a POST request to /api/service-profiles/{shopId} with the payload in testData, using a categoryId that does not exist.

Test Data: {"price": 100, "duration": 60, "categoryId": 9999, "shopId": 1, "status": true}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 500 Internal Server Error (or 404 Not Found if handled more gracefully) and an error message 'Service Category Not Found!'. The service profile is not created.
